scope: Proposition 2.3 (Single and product monodromy) of the manuscript “Quaternionic division points on curves in the Siegel threefold” (preprints/Quaternionic-Division-Points-on-Curves-in-the-Siegel-Threefold-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 016 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 e11b4b068502ced9), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 7. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For the family over any fixed smooth finite cover of a Hodge-generic curve in A2, the connected algebraic monodromy on H is Sp4, and that on V is SO(V, q). The same holds after pullback by a dominant morphism from an irreducible complex algebraic variety, on a smooth open of a resolution. Let S1, S2 be two such curves, and let an irreducible complex algebraic variety W map dominantly to both. On the sum of the two pulled-back weight-one systems, either the connected monodromy is Sp4 × Sp4, or the image of W in the product of the two moduli curves is contained in a dominating component of a polarized isogeny correspondence. In the latter case the corresponding local period relation is given by a fixed element of GSp4(Q) with positive multiplier.
